memory_update.text: Use PWR as the reference leader for grid field execution and backlog benchmarking, not as the main underfollowed alpha candidate.

POWL is a high-relevance electrical-distribution equipment candidate for the node, but its market cap has moved above the ideal USD 300M-10B discovery band; keep only if exposure purity remains unusually strong.
ATKR is a second-order electrical-infrastructure product candidate; validate whether data-center/electrification volume is material enough to offset commodity and construction-cycle exposure.

NVEE is a permitting/engineering/geospatial candidate for the execution bottleneck; survival in later layers depends on evidence that utility and data-center power work is material, not merely a small contract headline.

Layer 1B still needs a deeper search for transformer-component, protection-relay, utility-testing, galvanizing/coatings, and inspection/certification names, including PLPC, AZZ, HUBB, MTZ, and nVent, if candidate capacity is expanded beyond four.

POWL is a reference anchor for custom medium-voltage switchgear and packaged electrical systems in data-center, utility, LNG, and industrial power projects; use for pricing and backlog comparison, not as the main underfollowed hunt.
MYRG is an underfollowed grid-execution candidate with direct T&D, substation, clean-energy, EV charging, and data-center C&I exposure; monitor backlog quality and labor/project execution risk.

ATKR is a second-order electrical-products/components candidate tied to conduit, cable management, and infrastructure materials for commercial, industrial, data-center, solar, and telecom applications; verify end-market mix and price normalization.
WLDN is a small-cap underfollowed engineering and utility-program candidate for the permitting/planning/energy-efficiency layer of regulated grid and public-sector electrification spending.

IESC, TTEK, NVEE, ACM, MTZ, and EME should be screened in adjacent Layer 1B/1C passes, but were excluded here due to the four-candidate limit and to preserve focus on reference plus underfollowed grid/permitting execution names.

The most relevant bottleneck signals for this node are not just announced government spending, but backlog conversion, utility/customer award timing, interconnection-related project delays, switchgear and transformer lead times, permitting capacity, qualified labor availability, and margin durability.

POWL is a useful reference anchor for medium-voltage switchgear and electrical distribution bottlenecks, but its June 2026 market cap above $10B and increasing attention make it less suitable for the underfollowed lane.

WLDN is a low-attention services candidate for policy-to-project conversion: utility programs, government infrastructure, grid modernization, energy consulting, and possible permitting/interconnection adjacency.
MYRG maps directly to power-delivery field execution: transmission, distribution, substations, commercial/industrial electrical work, and data-center electrical demand.

AMRC is a small-cap distributed-energy and government/federal infrastructure candidate whose relevance increases if data centers and public agencies use microgrids or onsite power to bypass grid constraints.

Further Layer 1B passes should search for US-listed transformer component suppliers, relay/protection/testing vendors, NETA electrical testing firms, environmental permitting consultants, and privately held bottlenecks with public parents.

PWR should remain the reference leader for grid field execution, but it is high-attention and mega-cap; do not let it crowd out smaller specialty contractors and permitting consultants in later layers.

MYRG is a strong underfollowed Layer 1B candidate for transmission, distribution, substation, and data-center electrical construction exposure, with backlog and segment disclosures suitable for Layer 2 verification.

POWL is a useful power-equipment chokepoint candidate because its electric-utility, commercial/industrial, and data-center exposure maps to switchgear and electrical distribution constraints below the better-known mega-cap OEMs.
TTEK should be tracked as a permitting and regulatory-execution candidate; the key unresolved issue is whether grid and transmission permitting are material enough to consolidated results.

Potential next-pass names not included due to the 4-candidate limit: PRIM for utility/power-delivery construction, PLPC for transmission-line hardware and formed-wire components, NVEE for utility/geospatial/engineering services, ICFI for utility program and policy implementation, ATKR for electrical raceway/conduit, and HUBB as a larger electrical-grid component reference.
